archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (balanced, line-driven)
archetype.definition: A 4-4 team whose down-to-down efficiency sits near the top of the league, but whose special teams, giveaways and close-game results have cost it the wins its play has earned.

report.headline: A top-six team by EPA, wearing a .500 record from turnovers and special teams
report.take:
The Rams are 4-4 and play like a team with a better record. Their net EPA ranks 6th, they lead the league in yards per game at 400.3, and the defense ranks 8th in EPA allowed. The point differential says they should have about 5.6 wins. Their wins over expected of -1.59 ranks 30th. That gap has a cause: three of the losses were coin flips. They lost 26-30 at Denver, 34-37 to Buffalo, and 16-18 to Arizona as 12.5-point favorites. Only the opener against San Francisco, 7-27, was a beating.

The engine is the offensive line. It allows the league's 2nd-lowest pressure rate, has the lowest stuff rate in the NFL, and the run game averages 4.73 yards a carry. That lets McVay play the way he wants: a pass rate over expected that ranks 5th, a 4th-down go rate that ranks 1st, and a top-five success rate. Stafford's protection holds even though the time to throw is long, and the offense hasn't needed explosive passing every week to move the ball. The defense is built the opposite way from most good units. It barely gets home (25th in pressure rate, 27th in sacks), but it is the best in football against the deep ball and ranks 5th on both third down and red-zone touchdown rate. This is a bend-don't-break group that wins late in the down and close to the goal line.

The numbers hide what's leaking. Special teams are dead last at -3.86 EPA a game, and the turnover margin is -4 for the season. The offense has given the ball away 12 times, with two giveaways in five of the eight games. Those are exactly the hidden points that flip one-score games, and the 0.25 one-score win rate is the result. Turnover margin and close-game record tend to drift back toward the middle. Special teams this bad can be partly structural, and the long snapper is now out.

This isn't new territory for the McVay Rams. In 2023 and 2024 they won 10 games with middling efficiency and positive luck. Last year's 12-win team ranked 1st in net EPA. This team sits between those two: less explosive than 2025, but far sounder than its record. The concern is health. Stafford is nursing arm soreness, Adams is on IR, both starting corners left the last game, and two tight ends are banged up. The schedule tightens after this week too, with Green Bay, Kansas City and a trip to San Francisco in a row.

strengths.title: An offensive line that wins everything
strengths.body: The Rams allow pressure on just 16.6% of dropbacks, 2nd in the league, and their 14.4% stuff rate is the best in football. That shows up in a 4.73 yards-per-carry run game and the No. 1 yardage offense. Line play like this is the most repeatable part of a team, and it gives McVay's aggressive calling a stable floor.

strengths.title: Efficiency well ahead of the record
strengths.body: A 6th-ranked net EPA and a point differential that implies 5.6 wins say this is a good team that has lost the close ones. The losses at Denver and to Buffalo and Arizona came down to a possession, and only the SF opener was decisive. Close-game luck at 30th in wins over expected tends to even out.

strengths.title: Coverage that closes off the deep ball
strengths.body: The defense ranks 1st in deep-pass EPA allowed and 5th in short-pass EPA. It holds opponents to a 31% third-down rate and a 44.4% red-zone touchdown rate, both 5th. It does this without a pass rush, which means the back end is carrying it. That holds up only as long as the corners are healthy.

concerns.title: Hidden yards: turnovers and special teams
concerns.body: The Rams are last in the league in special-teams EPA per game and 27th in turnover differential, with 12 giveaways. These are the plays that decided their one-score losses. Turnover luck usually regresses, but the special teams problem looks more stubborn, and losing long snapper Joe Cardona makes it riskier in the short term.

concerns.title: No pass rush to speak of
concerns.body: A 20.9% pressure rate (25th) and 10 sacks (27th) put the whole defensive load on the coverage, and it explains why takeaways are scarce at 24th. Myles Garrett has played one game and is on track to practice. His return is the single biggest upgrade available to this defense.

concerns.title: Health at QB, corner and receiver
concerns.body: Stafford has taken 98% of the snaps and is listed questionable with arm soreness. Adams is out until late November, and McDuffie and Watson both left the Chargers game. If the corners miss time, a defense that already gives up production to slot receivers gets thinner.

trend.note: Results have swung week to week (L, W, L, W, L, L, W, W), and the passing game has run hot and cold. Two of its best passing-EPA games came alongside its worst. Underneath that, the line and the defense have been consistent, and the last two games were comfortable wins.

nextGame.headline: A good-not-great Rams team at a leaky Washington defense
nextGame.body:
The Book has the Rams -5.5 at Washington with a total of 47.5, and that's about right. Washington's defense ranks 25th in EPA allowed and 26th against the pass. It ranks 32nd in red-zone touchdown rate allowed and 25th on third down, and offenses pass against it more than against anyone else. Those are the exact situations where the Rams' efficient, pass-leaning offense lives. Washington does have one real defensive asset: it rarely gives up explosive runs (2nd) and is stingy on short passes. The Rams will probably have to finish drives rather than hit chunk plays. On the other side, Washington's offense is middle of the pack and its line allows the 28th-ranked pressure rate. A Rams pass rush that rarely gets home has a rare chance to win up front.

Availability shapes everything here. Stafford's arm is the headline: he is questionable, and Stetson Bennett is the only other passer to see action. The Rams are without Adams and tight end Parkinson, McDuffie and Watson are questionable at corner, and the long snapper is out. Garrett and tight end Ferguson are both trending toward practice. Washington is missing much more in the trenches. Payne and Kinlaw are out and Newton is on IR, which strips its interior defensive line. McLaurin and Tunsil are on IR as well. Washington's injuries are deeper, but the Rams' could matter more if Stafford is limited.

waysToWin.title: Nacua and the tight ends in coverage
waysToWin.body: Washington allows 0.44 EPA per target to opposing WR1s (25th) and 0.45 to TE1s (29th). Tight ends have scored 9.1 PPR points a game over their usual average against it, the worst in the league. With Adams out, Nacua and Higbee are the obvious targets for an offense that already passes more than expected.

waysToWin.title: Finish drives in the red zone
waysToWin.body: Washington gives up touchdowns on 81.8% of red-zone trips, the worst rate in the league. The Rams' defense ranks 5th in red-zone touchdown rate allowed. If both trends hold, the Rams turn similar drive counts into more points.

waysToWin.title: Lean on the line against a gutted interior
waysToWin.body: With three interior defensive linemen sidelined, the league's best run-blocking front by stuff rate should control the ball. That protects a possibly sore Stafford arm and keeps Washington's offense off the field.

waysToLose.title: Losing the turnover battle again
waysToLose.body: Washington is 3rd in turnover differential and the Rams are 27th. That mismatch is how a less efficient team steals a game, and it has already cost the Rams close results this year. Two more giveaways and a short field could erase the efficiency edge.

waysToLose.title: Stafford's arm limits the passing game
waysToLose.body: If the arm soreness restricts Stafford or forces Bennett into the game, the Rams lose the passing game they would use to attack Washington. Washington's short-pass defense ranks 6th, so a dink-and-dunk plan is not a sure thing. In their two worst passing-EPA games, the opener and the Chargers game, the offense managed 7 and 24 points.

waysToLose.title: A special-teams swing
waysToLose.body: The Rams have the league's worst special-teams unit and will play without their long snapper. A botched snap, a missed kick or a return touchdown is a realistic way for this game to tighten, much as the Arizona upset did.

nextGame.watch: Stafford's practice status and how the Rams use Higbee against a Washington defense that has been the worst in the league against tight ends.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the record to start catching up to the play. The line and the defense's coverage are the kind of strengths that hold up over a season. A -4 turnover margin and a 0.25 one-score win rate are the kind of numbers that drift toward neutral. Garrett's return would address the defense's one structural flaw. The special teams are the part least likely to fix itself, especially with a backup snapper.

The path isn't easy. After Washington and Arizona come Green Bay, Kansas City and a trip to San Francisco, followed by two games against Seattle's 5th-ranked defense and Tampa Bay's 2nd-ranked unit. Even so, a team this efficient should win most of its remaining games. That makes a wild-card berth the likely outcome and a run at the division a long shot behind 6-1 San Francisco. The range depends heavily on Stafford's arm.
swingFactors: Garrett's return to the pass rush
Whether turnovers and special teams stop bleeding points

confidence.note: The efficiency profile is clear after eight games, but Stafford's health and injuries at corner and receiver cloud the outlook.
